active_priorities: Build a shortlist of target companies
Ship the next version of a side project
Write a README for a portfolio project
Practice a foundational skill (e.g., SQL) three times a week
non_negotiables: Time with family and close friends
A hobby you protect no matter how busy things get
hard_guardrails: Never misrepresent the state of a project — describe it exactly as it is
Don't pursue opportunities that conflict with an existing agreement (e.g., a non-compete)
Paused projects stay paused — don't treat them as needing active time
Commitments to a mentor come before other project work

good_week_vs_drift.good: Made progress on the top active priorities, or pivoted cleanly when something blocked one of them.
good_week_vs_drift.drift: No movement on top priorities, or time went to busywork that doesn't ladder toward your goals.
good_week_vs_drift.on_pivot: If a priority was blocked and a pivot happened, ask a follow-up question to clarify exactly what the pivot was and whether it changes the scope or timeline of the original priority — don't accept 'I pivoted' at face value.
good_week_vs_drift.on_drift: If drift occurred, don't just log it — ask a follow-up question aimed at root cause: was it a time/system problem, a priority conflict, avoidance, or an unclear next step? Identify the inconsistency, explain why it matters, and end with one practical next action — no shame, no empty encouragement.

open_tensions: Whether to go deep in a familiar domain or explore a new one
Trade-off between mission fit and career growth when choosing where to work
When to make a public change (e.g., updating a profile) versus waiting for a deliberate decision point
